speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: With 13 straight years of ridership expansion, Singaporeans are highly dependent on this public good.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government's drive towards a car-lite society creates a stronger imperative for a seamlessly working public transport system.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The feedback from the ground on the most recent Fare Review Exercise has presented us in this House with a timely opportunity to look critically at our public transportation system.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Our starting point must be to put our commuters first over other stakeholders and be world-class leaders in areas, such as reliability, affordability and quality.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On the issue of rail reliability, not too long ago, Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) breakdowns became a familiar, yet unwelcome part of our news cycle.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Our bus services were inadequate to fully run parallel to our train systems, and private bus operators had to be called in to help with some of the major breakdowns in the past few years.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government has more recently injected public funds to nationalise our public transportation assets and infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Various schemes were rolled out, aimed at expanding and upgrading its public transportation infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One can only imagine what would have happened if the Government had not chosen to invest and kept to its previous stance of leaving entirely to market forces.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But train delays are not really a thing of the past, as can be seen in the recent train delays late last year and early this year.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Let us also not forget that the latest MKBF statistics did not include delays caused by the signalling works which the Singapore MRT (SMRT) and Land Transport Authority (LTA) have reportedly agreed to exclude, nor did it include delays of not more than five minutes.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: MKBF measures delays of more than five minutes.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Notwithstanding their exclusion from the internationally used MKBF benchmark, commuters may still have lingering doubts on the reliability of our MRT system if we completely disregard delays of not more than five minutes.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: MKBF is also an operational metric that may not truly measure the convenience to passengers, a point made in a 2013 Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) International Transport Forum discussion paper entitled "Measuring and Valuing Convenience and Service Quality".

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The authors also mentioned that measuring delays from a more customer-focused perspective requires appropriate data collected in a sufficient level of detail, such as number of passengers affected and passenger hours delay.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Such data do not seem to be within the public sphere currently and will be necessary if we are to move towards a holistic commuter-centric public transport system.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In other words, convenience and service quality should be measured and reported.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: With such big investments as I have mentioned earlier, the affordability of fares is crucial.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even as we are second among 12 cities in affordability from a recent Nanyang Technological University study, our focus should be on Singaporeans and how they are impacted by fare prices.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Indeed, the yearly review of transportation fares by the Public Transport Council (PTC) is always closely watched by the public.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even as the Government has argued the case for NCF, there are many other views expressed about this new component.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One Straits Times' reader expressed that this factor is akin to taxing commuters twice.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Current Nominated Member of Parliament, the hon Assoc Prof Walter Theseira, opined that the factor makes a rise in fares more likely, as capacity will rise faster than ridership in the short term.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Straits Times' Senior Transport Correspondent Mr Christopher Tan also pointed out the irony that a negative NCF will imply more crowded buses and trains, an outcome that no commuter wants to see.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Perhaps the Minister can share on how the Ministry of Transport (MOT) intends to help such individuals transit to cashless payments.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Our public transportation system needs to deliver on quality, most important of which is the punctuality of services and the minimising of all delays.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Beyond that, it will also require timely and accurate information to be delivered by operators on matters of relevance, such as service disruptions, minimising bus bunching, ensuring a comfortable ride and cost-effectively, improving physical comfort, such as improving ventilation on our open-air MRT stations and bus interchanges.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We understand that current service quality lapses are penalised with fines, but have these fines exercised a sufficient deterrent effect thus far, including delays of not more than five minutes?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There may be scope to include service quality in our fare regulation framework to incentivise public transport operators (PTOs) to work actively on service quality and to maintain a higher standard in these areas.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: All of the above requires entrenching a service culture among our operators, one that places the commuters at the heart of everything they do.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is, of course, easier said than done.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Our public transport personnel need to be understanding when facing problems and take flak from disgruntled commuters with a smile.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: At this point, I wish to put on record the sincere appreciation we in the Workers' Party have for all public transport workers tirelessly working to ensure that our systems are running smoothly.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Many Singaporeans spend a good part of their lives on public transport.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As a public good that is inextricably tied to quality of life and is critical for our economy, we must spare no effort in evaluating all transport policies to ensure that we put our commuters first and be class-leading in reliability, affordability and quality.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Here, I would like to put forth some suggestions for MOT to consider in improving our public transportation system moving forward.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Alongside an expansion of MKBF metrics, we can be more holistic in our approach to measure reliability.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Seeing that SMRT is part of the Community of Metros (CoMET), we can also get our rail PTOs to work towards a full implementation of the CoMET scorecard, with disclosure of its results on a yearly basis to the public.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Covering areas, such as customer, environment, safety and so on, it is a balanced approach to understand the public transport system and align operator incentives to improve our public transport system beyond just the current singular metric that is operationally focused.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: LTA and PTC do run surveys to gather feedback.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A recent survey for the 2040 Land Transport Master Plan has concluded that commuters prize convenience the most in Singapore’s land transport system, followed by connectivity and fast travel time.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, the survey did not touch on the reliability and affordability of our future public transport.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As for service quality, while LTA and PTC do run surveys of customer satisfaction for public transport, the numbers of satisfied commuters look very high compared to a similar survey run by the Institute of Service Excellence (ISE).

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, in November 2016, the Government said that PTC had excluded service quality as a factor from the Fare Review formula as the plan was for the Government to, I quote from Minister Khaw Boon Wan in his answer to a Parliamentary Question on 7 November 2016, "regulate and work with the operators independently to improve service levels" and, in doing so, kept the – and I quote from Minister Khaw again – "fare formula relatively straightforward, without the complication of differentiating fare adjustments on account of service quality".

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe that a direct link between the ability to raise prices and service quality will help to improve the total commuter experience.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The inclusion of service quality as perceived by the commuters themselves, realistically measured by an independent body, can help mitigate the risk of operators raising fares as a result of pursuing other goals at the expense of service quality.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I should emphasise that service quality should be merely one of the factors and not the only or predominant factor.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Some may argue that with the recent improvements we have seen in MKBF, it is unnecessary to link fare review to service quality.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, if MKBF and overall service quality are both truly improving, that is all the more reason why now is a good time to introduce service quality as a factor in the annual Fare Review exercise to ensure that service quality will keep improving and not go backwards in future.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The size of operating profits derived from both transport and transport-related lines of business, such as retail operations, should be one of the factors considered in allowing fares to be raised but not the only or predominant factor.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: To any who may proffer the superficial view that this would create a perverse incentive for PTOs to run their outfits in such a way as to lower profits, so as to be allowed to raise fares, my reply would be that no reasonable profit maximising company would deliberately lower profitability so as to increase the chances of being allowed to raise fares when the linkage between profitability and fare review is small and indirect.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In a public consultation in Hong Kong on FAM in 2016, the Hong Kong government noted that (a) a majority of the public submissions requested that the profitability of the MTR Corporation should be reflected in the FAM, (b) when the profit of the MTR Corporation in a particular year reaches a certain level, the MTR Corporation should not increase fares", and (c) a new "profit factor", which reflects the profit made in a particular year, should be added to the existing FAM formula to reduce fare increases.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Hong Kong's experience can offer insights into how Singapore can go about tweaking our Fare Regulation Framework to account for newly proposed factors.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is possible for us to factor in profit via the current Productivity Extraction Factor.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This would be to redefine or tweak the current definition to account for the PTOs' profitability.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since Productivity as a factor is a minus, any increase in this factor would lead to a lower fare hike for commuters and will be more equitable for commuters.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The extent of profits in an oligopolistic, highly regulated industry with huge barriers to entry like public transport cannot and should not be completely irrelevant to the ability to raise fares.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Third, there is room for PTOs to put in more of their profits from their operations into our various funds investing in long-term public transport quality.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A further step can be taken in this regard.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Retail operations in MRT stations will not be profitable without the infrastructure in or around the stations.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Mandating a level of profits from retail operations to be added to the Railway Sinking Fund and the Rail Infrastructure Fund will move us towards a more equitable development of our infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Having benefited from the fleet expansion through the Bus Service Enhancement Programme (BSEP), a similar profit transfer mechanism can also apply to our bus operators leasing and operating the various bus interchanges.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Fourth, timely information is needed about service disruptions and planned early closing announcements.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There are still many commuters that are less technologically inclined and may not have the needed apps installed.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We can consider a multi-channel, multi-platform and multilingual approach to send out broadcast messages on service disruptions, planned early closings and late openings, for example, via electronic notice boards and radio, not unlike what the Ministry of Home Affairs has done with alerts in times of emergencies.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Information that is being piped out must be both timely and accurate.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Complaints of inaccurate estimated waiting time, information about alternative bus arrangements and even lack of reports of delays by PTOs are common over social media.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government should work to ensure that such complaints will become a thing of the past.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Lastly, while the bulk of the attention is now rightly given to our oldest two lines, we should not forget that our other lines are reaching their age milestones as well.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, a convenient and efficient public transport system is critical to our city, people and economy.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: To become a car-lite, clean, beautiful and liveable city, public transport must be people's prime mode of transportation.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: To build a convenient and efficient public transport system, reliability, affordability and quality are three important factors.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Rail reliability is a continuous work in progress.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We noticed that the Government has, indeed, increased investment in rail assets and infrastructures, and there was improvement in MKBF in 2018.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, there is a drawback by focusing on MKBF only, because it means that we are only paying attention to delays of more than five minutes and ignoring those delays that are less than five minutes.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Last year, when we reviewed the Fare Review Formula, a new factor was included as one of the considerations, and that is the network capacity which shows the commuter volume and usage rate.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is to better reflect the changes in operating cost.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We must pay close attention to the impact of fare hikes on the vulnerable groups.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We need to ensure that the public transport system can provide high-quality services, such as physical comfort, timely and accurate information.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Here, the Workers’ Party would like to thank all our public transport workers.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The public transport system is critical to our economic and social development.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We must spare no effort to improve the system.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Hence, I would like to put forth five suggestions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: First, engage third-party independent bodies to conduct investigations, and use a scorecard system and service quality as part of the Fare Review formula.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This will not only incentivise the operators but also monitor the overall reliability and service quality.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Third, put back a level of profits from retail operations into the Railway Sinking Fund and the Rail Infrastructure Fund.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Fourth, adopt a multi-channel, multi-platform and multilingual approach to send out timely and accurate messages about service disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I was worried as he began that he was about to deliver my Committee of Supply speech on my behalf because I heard that he wanted to put commuters first – so do I; that he wanted to thank public transport workers – so do I; that he believes that reliability, quality and affordability are important components of our public transport system – so do I.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, I take it the Member agrees that we have a world-class public transport system and it is largely supported by the models and the direction, the efforts that we are making and I thank him for his kind words.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Member has made some suggestions about how we can improve, and these suggestions are worth examining as we have to consider how we can achieve the aims that we have set out and that he agrees with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Any suggestions for improving our public transport system, there are a few preconditions that we have to think of first as we assess.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The first is: do we have existing mechanisms?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In truth, every mechanism has a cost – a cost in time, a cost in compliance burden, a financial cost, and cost effectiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Thirdly, we should ask, "How are Singaporeans responding?" How is our system responding?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Before we get into that, we might also ask, "Are we actually already doing some of the things that Mr Dennis Tan is suggesting or anybody is suggesting?" For some of the examples that Mr Dennis Tan is talking about, there is a financial basis to incentivise better operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: You can look at it from the profit point of view, you can look at it from the fare point of view, you can look at penalties, you can look at it as where you redistribute it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But essentially, you are using money to incentivise better behaviour on the part of the operators and taking some of that money and rewarding commuters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, there are two arms to it – financial penalties or financial rewards, and then how you return it to the system or the commuters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Frankly, as the Member has described in great detail, we are doing that in a number of ways, across a number of mechanisms, using a variety of models with different operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Are we trying to get more information out to commuters that are affected?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Certainly, we can do a lot better and we will continue to experiment and to attempt to service Singaporeans better as they take public transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I would start by saying, firstly, MKBF is not the only metric that we use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Dennis Tan suggested that we should broaden our consideration of what counts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are a whole bunch of other things that we do in our regulatory framework as we interface with the operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have maintenance performance standards, operating performance standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These are codified, they are written down, they are agreed upon and, as a result of which, LTA and the operators work very closely together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have engineers who are embedded in the operator teams; reports come up to us on a regular basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Failure at any one of these points can result in a financial penalty, as the Member has described on my behalf.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These frameworks, we can tighten them on a regular basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: LTA has been tightening them and adjusting them and making them more effective on a regular basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have used models, such as the BSEP, to increase the capacity for buses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have invested in engineering capacity, we have invested in how to develop capability locally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These are all a variety of mechanisms to improve reliability and improve quality as we put commuters at the heart of the experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: On top of that, we have worked quite hard around inclusion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have tried to make sure that it is not just about the capacity, not just about what we can do technically, but also how we can reach out to a greater number of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, all MRT stations have two access routes which are barrier free, wheelchair-accessible lifts, all trains have wheelchair space, all bus interchanges are barrier-free, we are able to do wheelchair boarding, wheelchair-accessible toilets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is not to say that we have done everything.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have not completed upgrading all the bus stops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are bus stops that are not entirely wheelchair-accessible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have installed nearly 50 lifts at pedestrian overhead bridges as well as 200 km of covered linkways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are moving aggressively to make sure that public transport is available and accessible to an increasing number of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have committed to making sure that eight in 10 households will be living within a 10-minute walk to the MRT station.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have been increasing the number of rail lines, the number of trains as we move along that journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have increased capacity – buses, trains, rail lines – carrying capacity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have increased inclusivity: more and more Singaporeans are able to access our public transport system and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Dennis Tan is concentrating on the most recent fare review.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But on average, we take a slightly broader view.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Over the last five years, fares have gone down by 1.2%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: On balance, the amount that people spend on fares out of their household income has gone down.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It has gone down for the second quintile, and the second decile.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And we know that, on average, expenditure as a proportion of your income has gone down.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The biggest single group are seniors, and that will only continue to rise as our population slowly ages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But students, full-time National Servicemen, low-wage workers, a whole lot.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, we have worked hard to make these mechanisms work for us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As Mr Dennis Tan has pointed out, these mechanisms are resulting in an increasing number of Singaporeans choosing to take public transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Year-on-year growth of ridership, a greater proportion of Singaporeans at peak hours choosing not to use private vehicles as their primary mode of transport and choosing to use shared public transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Satisfaction levels have risen in tandem as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: That would all suggest that we are moving in the right direction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Perhaps, we need to consider some mechanisms to make sure we maintain our trajectory.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But if we are already doing some or many of these things, we should refine them, get them right, tweak them, make them better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But we have to start on the premise that things are improving, things are going well, the mechanisms are working and we do need to make sure that we hang on to our fundamental principles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: My fundamental principles, as it turns out, are very much similar to what Mr Dennis Tan has articulated, that we do this with the view to putting the commuter at the centre of the experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We focus on reliability, on quality, on affordability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And we make sure that, over time, over the long term, we do this in a fair way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Everybody needs to participate in it, and the help needs to be distributed to those who need it most.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have to have long-term financial viability and competitive participation, and we do this in an effective way around reliability, comfort and to continually increase the participation of Singaporeans in public transport.
